title: lmkd 日志、statsd 与 victim 分析：从 kill reason 到 adj/RSS
key_conclusions: lmkd logs and statsd records are the entry point for kill analysis, not a complete root-cause report.
A victim worksheet should align pressure, priority, memory cost, and source-bucket evidence at the kill timestamp.
statsd helps aggregate low-memory kills, while logcat and dumpsys preserve faster incident context.
RSS and kill benefit must be interpreted with PSS, memcg, shared buffers, ZRAM, and Day 53 bucket attribution.
shallow_points: The article does not include real lmkd log lines or statsd atoms from a device.
It does not validate log field names across Android versions and vendor builds.
It does not include a parser for statsd protobuf output.
It does not quantify how RSS, PSS, and swap change after a victim is killed.
discovered_connections: Day 56's three-line model becomes a worksheet with pressure, priority, cost, and source fields.
Day 55 OomAdjuster evidence explains whether the logged adj was expected.
Day 53 bucket attribution prevents over-blaming the killed process.
Day 58 should explain how ZRAM and swap change the apparent benefit and latency cost of kills.
suggest_future_topics: Day 58 should connect ZRAM mm_stat, swap-in/out, compression, and latency to victim analysis.
Day 61 should build a collector script for lmkd logs, PSI, meminfo, vmstat, ZRAM, and adj snapshots.
Day 65 should use the victim worksheet in a complete high-priority kill case study.
A future tool should parse statsd low-memory kill atoms into the worksheet format.
knowledge_gaps: Need real statsd low-memory kill samples and field mapping.
Need Android branch validation for lmkd log strings and reason enums.
Need vendor examples where kill reason formatting differs.
Need before/after datasets showing kill benefit in RSS, PSS, swap, PSI, and user recovery.
